changes: Encrypted send/edit requests capture a local receipt boundary before POST/PATCH. Their matching HTTP response may claim a cache-write guard only when no newer different source or deletion has been observed. A matching WS echo shares its existing token, so pending echo publication is not cancelled by its own HTTP response.

Receipt source identity includes conversation, message, author, device, ciphertext and metadata. HTTP source validation now checks sender_device_id as well as the previously checked prepared source fields. A later accepted receipt/event invalidates previous write guards across asynchronous hash/storage preparation.

Superseded/deleted send/edit receipts discard only their exact local pending payload. A successfully committed HTTP operation remains successful even if a subsequent edit/delete prevents caching its old text. No automatic POST retry or encryption downgrade added.
verification: Focused API-consumer, WS, version and cache suites passed: 4 files / 88 tests. Added live edit/delete/matching-echo send receipts, abandoned edit receipts, device mismatch, token sharing, generation/conversation scope, overlapping receipt guards, and real SHA-256 async cache-write races.
Final tsc -b and targeted ESLint passed.

Full client suite passed: 232 files / 2293 tests in 47.60s. Vite production build passed in 714ms with existing build warnings. Targeted diff whitespace and coverage validation passed: 33 references / 261 behaviors; acceptance remains incomplete.
